show-example.label: Show example
show-example.description: Show the small starter example for this step.

explain-why.label: Explain why
explain-why.description: Explain the purpose and what becomes weaker if this step is compressed or skipped.

show-canonical-method.label: Show canonical method
show-canonical-method.description: Show the profile-specific method, schedule, selected method, and fidelity impact.

show-checklist.label: Show checklist
show-checklist.description: Show dependencies, what good looks like, and the complete definition-of-done checklist.

compare-substitutes.label: Compare substitutes
compare-substitutes.description: Compare approved substitutes and their method and evidence trade-offs.

i-am-blocked.label: I am blocked
i-am-blocked.description: Show likely failure modes, approved workarounds, and the smallest useful next action.

pause.label: Pause
pause.description: Record a resumable pause without inventing progress or crossing a human gate.

01-intake.title: Intake
01-intake.whyItMatters: A clear decision frame prevents the sprint from producing a polished answer to the wrong problem.
01-intake.purpose: Frame the consequential challenge, intended outcome, constraints, evidence, and unknowns before committing to a sprint.

methods.sprint-book: Pre-sprint challenge intake and Decider alignment

01-intake.humanEffort: Answer one focused question at a time and correct the drafted brief.
01-intake.humanAction: Describe what you need to create, change, or decide and why it matters now.
aiRole: Draft the brief from supplied context
Identify the single highest-value missing input
dependencies: An initial challenge or decision to frame
whatGoodLooksLike: The brief is specific enough to guide a route decision
Known evidence and unresolved assumptions are easy to distinguish
definitionOfDone: Challenge and likely customer are explicit
Outcome, constraints, evidence, unknowns, and deadline are recorded
examples: Improve onboarding for first-time team admins so they can invite a colleague without support.
failureModes: Demanding a polished brief before starting
Framing a deliverable instead of the decision or outcome
limitations: A partial intake leaves route selection and later evidence work less reliable
Skipping intake can optimize the wrong challenge

substitutes.name: Evidence-led draft for human correction
substitutes.useWhen: The Decider has supplied documents but little time for an interview.
substitutes.preserves: A concrete brief and explicit human correction.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Compresses live alignment into asynchronous review.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: Missing tacit constraints remain unknown until the human corrects the draft.

02-qualify.title: Qualify and route
02-qualify.whyItMatters: Choosing the route deliberately focuses effort on the uncertainty that can actually change the decision.
02-qualify.purpose: Choose a route that matches the uncertainty instead of applying sprint ceremony by default.
02-qualify.humanEffort: Review one route recommendation and approve, revise, or stop.
02-qualify.humanAction: Choose the route, method profile, and execution mode after reviewing their trade-offs.
aiRole: Assess evidence sufficiency and decision uncertainty independently
Recommend a route with limitations and customer needs
dependencies: Explicit human selector for method profile and execution mode
whatGoodLooksLike: The recommendation follows from the evidence and decision uncertainty
The human can see what the route includes, excludes, and requires
definitionOfDone: Route and rationale are recorded
Human involvement, recruitment needs, and exclusions are visible
Gate 1 has an explicit human decision
examples: Recommend research-first because the customer and problem are not yet evidenced; reroute after the research stage.
failureModes: Choosing the full route because it sounds more rigorous
Treating self-test or rehearsal as customer evidence
limitations: A weak route decision can add ceremony without reducing uncertainty
The one-human-plus-AI team does not reproduce a cross-functional human team

substitutes.name: Short evidence-and-uncertainty review
substitutes.useWhen: A full readiness workshop is impractical.
substitutes.preserves: Explicit route choice tied to evidence and decision uncertainty.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Compresses team readiness discussion into bounded independent assessments.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: Unrepresented stakeholder constraints may remain unknown.

03-evidence.title: Build the evidence base
03-evidence.whyItMatters: Early evidence reduces assumption-driven design, while starting recruitment now protects the longest-lead part of live testing.
03-evidence.purpose: Create shared understanding from relevant knowledge and evidence before solution generation.

methods.sprint-book: Expert interviews, shared knowledge, and How Might We notes
methods.adaptive-design-sprint: Sourced evidence review and early recruitment planning

03-evidence.humanEffort: Provide private context, resolve material source conflicts, and approve the recruitment target, screener, owner, and next action.
03-evidence.humanAction: Confirm the reliable evidence and launch the smallest approved recruitment action now.
aiRole: Build a sourced evidence ledger
Draft the complete neutral recruitment plan and detect stalled progress
dependencies: Live route: recruitment owner, suitable target, channels, consent expectations, and deadline
whatGoodLooksLike: Claims are traceable to sources, with contradictions and gaps visible
The live recruitment plan is neutral, practical, owned, and ready for its next action without depending on a paid vendor
definitionOfDone: Sources, contradictions, and gaps are recorded
Live route has a usable target definition, neutral screener, outreach and reminder templates, schedule, consent checklist, and backup plan
Live route has an explicit owner and next action
examples: Target people who personally completed the relevant workflow in the past 30 days; exclude colleagues, conflicted participants, and respondents who cannot describe a recent instance.
failureModes: Waiting until the prototype is finished to recruit
Writing a screener that names the preferred solution
Assuming a paid panel is the only route
limitations: AI synthesis adds no firsthand evidence
Incomplete recruitment can delay testing and later produces only the partial evidence classification implemented by the four-dimensional completion model

substitutes.name: Bounded expert inputs plus sourced review
substitutes.useWhen: Canonical live expert interviews and shared team knowledge are unavailable.
substitutes.preserves: Relevant knowledge becomes traceable and shared before solution work.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Replaces a live cross-functional exercise with asynchronous inputs.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: Quality depends on available sources and expert access; missing operational knowledge stays unknown.

04-foundation.title: Establish the foundation
04-foundation.whyItMatters: An explicit strategic hypothesis gives later solution work a coherent customer, problem, alternative, and reason to believe.
04-foundation.purpose: Establish a coherent customer, problem, advantage, alternative, and differentiation hypothesis when one does not yet exist.

methods.sprint-book: Not a separate Sprint-book exercise; use an established challenge and strategic context

04-foundation.humanEffort: Resolve material strategic conflicts and approve a testable founding hypothesis.
04-foundation.humanAction: Choose the customer/problem/differentiation hypothesis worth carrying into design.
aiRole: Draft evidence-labelled strategic elements
Challenge unsupported advantage and differentiation claims
dependencies: A route that includes the foundation stage
whatGoodLooksLike: Each strategic claim is evidence-labelled and internally coherent
The proposed differentiation is deliverable and falsifiable
definitionOfDone: Every hypothesis element has an evidence label
Differentiation is deliverable rather than aspirational
The founding hypothesis can be tested
examples: If we help independent clinic managers reconcile claims without spreadsheets, they will choose it over manual review because exceptions are explained at the point of action.
failureModes: Treating generic quality claims as differentiation
Hiding missing evidence behind a polished strategy statement
limitations: A foundation hypothesis is a proposal, not customer evidence
Skipping this stage on an unformed product makes later solution comparison arbitrary

substitutes.name: Existing strategy audit
substitutes.useWhen: A current strategic brief already exists.
substitutes.preserves: Explicit customer, problem, alternatives, advantage, and testable differentiation.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Uses reviewed existing decisions instead of creating a new foundation artifact from scratch.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: Stale or unevidenced assumptions must remain labelled and may require investigation.

05-map.title: Map the experience
05-map.whyItMatters: A shared view of actors, handoffs, and failure points reveals where an intervention can change the outcome.
05-map.purpose: Build shared understanding of the customer journey or system and select the most consequential target moment.

methods.sprint-book: Map the challenge from actors to outcome and select a target

05-map.humanEffort: Correct the map and choose the moment where change would matter most.
05-map.humanAction: Select the target moment on the merged customer and system map.
aiRole: Map the experience and technical dependencies separately
Merge the maps while preserving failure points and edge cases
whatGoodLooksLike: The map connects customer action to system and operational response
The selected target moment is consequential and supported by the evidence
definitionOfDone: Trigger, actors, journey, system responses, dependencies, and failures are explicit
One consequential target moment is selected
examples: Target the moment a new admin decides whether to invite teammates, before setup becomes a solo dead end.
failureModes: Mapping only interface screens
Selecting the easiest moment rather than the riskiest consequential moment
limitations: An inferred journey can omit real behavior
Compressing the map can hide operational handoffs and edge cases

substitutes.name: Critical-path map
substitutes.useWhen: A full journey workshop is impractical and the decision concerns one narrow flow.
substitutes.preserves: Actors, trigger, target moment, dependencies, failures, and outcome remain visible.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Compresses the breadth of canonical mapping.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: Adjacent journeys and secondary actors may remain unknown.

06-questions.title: Define sprint questions
06-questions.whyItMatters: Precommitted questions and signals keep the test focused on risks and make later interpretation harder to rewrite after the fact.
06-questions.purpose: Turn the long-term goal and riskiest assumptions into agreed questions and observable failure signals.

methods.sprint-book: Long-term goal, sprint questions, target selection, and Decider confirmation

06-questions.humanEffort: Review the ranked risks and approve the target questions and failure criteria.
06-questions.humanAction: Confirm which risks could genuinely make the idea fail.
aiRole: Rank assumptions independently by consequence, uncertainty, and testability
Turn top risks into observable questions and signals
whatGoodLooksLike: Questions concern consequential uncertainty rather than preference
Each question has observable success, ambiguity, and failure signals
definitionOfDone: Long-term goal and target are explicit
Ranked questions have observable success, ambiguity, and failure signals
Gate 2 is human-approved
examples: Can a target customer explain the value and choose a next step without the moderator teaching the concept?
failureModes: Asking whether users like the idea
Rewriting questions after results are known
limitations: Poorly observable questions produce opinion rather than behavioral evidence
Compressing independent risk ranking increases anchoring risk

substitutes.name: Independent risk memos plus human ranking
substitutes.useWhen: A live cross-functional risk workshop is unavailable.
substitutes.preserves: Multiple perspectives diverge before the Decider converges on observable risks.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Changes synchronous discussion into bounded independent assessments.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: AI assessments are proposals and do not supply stakeholder or customer evidence.

07-explore.title: Explore independently
07-explore.whyItMatters: Independent divergence reduces anchoring and gives the Decider concrete alternatives instead of one prematurely polished idea.
07-explore.purpose: Diverge independently into multiple concrete, evidence-aware solution directions before evaluating them.

methods.sprint-book: Lightning Demos followed by four-step sketching
methods.adaptive-design-sprint: Independent concrete solution directions with a sourced precedent scan

07-explore.humanEffort: Contribute or review concrete flows only after independent directions are complete.
07-explore.humanAction: Confirm that the directions are meaningfully different and concrete enough to test.
aiRole: Run a sourced precedent scan
Generate independent concrete flows from bounded specialist roles without cross-contamination
whatGoodLooksLike: Directions differ in mechanism, not only presentation
Each flow is concrete enough to expose a critical test scene and its assumptions
definitionOfDone: At least three meaningfully different concrete directions exist
Each direction names evidence, assumptions, risk, and a test scene
Dissent remains visible
examples: Show a four-scene flow with entry context, action, system response, and consequence—not a paragraph saying use AI.
failureModes: Producing cosmetic variants
Sharing the first recommendation before other roles diverge
Submitting prose-only ideas as sketches
limitations: AI-generated directions are proposals, not evidence
Missing human disciplines and lived experience can narrow the option set

substitutes.name: Sourced precedent scan plus independently generated concrete flows
substitutes.useWhen: Lightning Demos and multi-person four-step sketching are unavailable.
substitutes.preserves: Inspiration is sourced and concrete alternatives exist before convergence.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Replaces live human show-and-tell and sketching with bounded AI-assisted work.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: Precedents and generated flows do not demonstrate customer preference or stakeholder support.

08-decide.title: Compare and decide
08-decide.whyItMatters: Explicit criteria and a named Decider turn divergent work into one testable direction without hiding trade-offs or dissent.
08-decide.purpose: Converge deliberately on one coherent direction while keeping decision criteria, dissent, and rejected alternatives visible.

methods.sprint-book: Art museum, heat-map review, speed critique, straw poll, and Decider supervote
methods.adaptive-design-sprint: Independent role assessments followed by the human Decider

08-decide.humanEffort: Review the comparison and make one explicit consequential choice.
08-decide.humanAction: Choose one coherent direction and state the main reason, reservations, and any deliberate combination.
aiRole: Define criteria before revealing recommendations
Present comparison, trade-offs, and dissent without choosing
whatGoodLooksLike: The choice follows criteria fixed before recommendations were revealed
Rejected alternatives and material reservations remain visible
definitionOfDone: Criteria predate the choice
Selected and rejected directions and dissent are recorded
Gate 3 records the human decision
examples: Choose Direction B because it tests the highest-consequence trust risk with the fewest simulated steps.
failureModes: Counting AI assessments as votes
Combining every idea into an incoherent prototype
Hiding a material dissenting view
limitations: Assessment convergence is not stakeholder support or customer evidence
A single Decider may lack perspectives held by an absent human team

substitutes.name: Independent role assessments followed by the human Decider
substitutes.useWhen: A team heat map, critique, and straw poll are unavailable.
substitutes.preserves: Trade-offs are exposed and the Decider owns the final choice.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Substitutes structured analysis for human team voting mechanics.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: AI agreement cannot be interpreted as stakeholder or customer preference.

09-experiment.title: Design the experiment
09-experiment.whyItMatters: A bounded experiment connects the chosen direction to observable evidence before build effort makes the team defensive about the solution.
09-experiment.purpose: Translate the chosen direction into a fixed hypothesis, realistic storyboard, and observable test signals.

methods.sprint-book: Storyboard the customer test from opening scene through critical moments

09-experiment.humanEffort: Approve the hypothesis, lowest sufficient artifact rung, tool route, safety boundaries, and build approvals.
09-experiment.humanAction: Confirm that the scenes and approved prototype/MVP brief can answer the sprint questions.
aiRole: Draft scenes, scorecard, and realistic boundaries
Recommend the lowest sufficient artifact rung and provider-neutral tool route
dependencies: Approved prototype/MVP brief and tool decision from the #15 workflow
whatGoodLooksLike: Every scene earns its place by answering an approved sprint question
The lowest sufficient artifact rung, reality boundary, tool route, and approvals are explicit
definitionOfDone: Four to six scenes map to sprint questions
Signals and thresholds are fixed before testing
The typed prototype/MVP brief and applicable human approvals are complete
examples: Use a clickable four-scene facade because task comprehension matters; simulate persistence because repeated use is outside the question.
failureModes: Designing a demo instead of an experiment
Increasing fidelity because AI can build quickly
Requesting a vague build without approved scope and tool boundaries
limitations: A storyboard cannot answer behaviors it does not realistically expose
Unapproved or excessive fidelity adds cost, privacy, and operational risk without stronger evidence

substitutes.name: Four-to-six-scene experiment card
substitutes.useWhen: A room-scale storyboard exercise is impractical.
substitutes.preserves: The opening context, critical moments, questions, signals, and prototype boundary are fixed.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Compresses collaborative storyboarding into an explicit reviewable sequence.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: Missing perspectives can leave unrealistic context or omitted failure states.

10-prototype.title: Build and review the prototype
10-prototype.whyItMatters: A realistic but tightly bounded artifact lets customers encounter the critical experience without confusing build completeness with validation.
10-prototype.purpose: Build and trial-run the smallest realistic prototype capable of answering the agreed questions.

methods.sprint-book: Divide-and-conquer realistic prototype build plus trial run
methods.adaptive-design-sprint: Bounded prototype build with independent critique and research-readiness review

10-prototype.humanEffort: Authorize any external account, spend, data, or deployment action and approve Gate 4 after the real script passes a trial.
10-prototype.humanAction: Approve or reject the immutable trial-passed tested version for customer sessions.
aiRole: Build only from the #15 approved brief packet
Run separate critical and research-readiness reviews and document simulation
dependencies: Canonical test plan and moderated trial
whatGoodLooksLike: The approved critical scenes feel coherent while simulated boundaries remain explicit
The exact neutral protocol passes a trial and the tested version is immutable
definitionOfDone: Approved scenes work accessibly within the reality boundary
The actual neutral script passes a moderated trial
A tested version freezes prototype, plan, deployment, expiry, cleanup, rollback, and limitations
Gate 4 is human-approved
examples: Freeze proto-v1 only after the exact interview script runs end to end without teaching the concept.
failureModes: Building beyond the approved brief
Treating a live URL as validation
Using production data or spend without explicit human approval
Changing the script or prototype without a new version
limitations: A test-ready prototype is neither customer validation nor production readiness
Simulated behavior bounds what sessions can establish

substitutes.name: Single-builder bounded implementation plus independent reviews
substitutes.useWhen: A divide-and-conquer prototype team is unavailable.
substitutes.preserves: The approved scenes are built, trialled, critiqued, and frozen separately from the build claim.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Changes team production mechanics while retaining independent readiness checks.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: Reduced implementation diversity can miss issues; the trial and explicit limitations constrain later claims.

11-customer-sessions.title: Run real-customer sessions
11-customer-sessions.whyItMatters: Observing suitable customers using the same tested version produces evidence that internal opinions and simulated participants cannot supply.
11-customer-sessions.purpose: Observe suitable real customers encountering the prototype under a consistent protocol.

methods.sprint-book: Five one-to-one customer interviews observed by the sprint team
methods.adaptive-design-sprint: Planned one-to-one sessions with suitable real customers

11-customer-sessions.humanEffort: Confirm suitability and consent, conduct or authorize moderation, and keep session records accurate.
11-customer-sessions.humanAction: Run the next booked suitable participant session or activate the smallest recruitment backup action.
aiRole: Prepare isolated version-bound session packets
Support neutral moderation only with suitable tooling and consent
Record observation separately from inference
dependencies: Approved target, screener, consent, schedule, and backups
whatGoodLooksLike: Participants are suitable, consenting, and exposed to a consistent neutral protocol
Observation stays separate from inference and any target shortfall remains explicit
definitionOfDone: Recruitment and consent are documented
At least one suitable real session is complete
Protocol deviations and anonymized evidence are recorded
Target shortfall remains visible rather than silently lowered
examples: With three usable sessions from a five-session plan, mark testing partial directional, activate backups, and retain the original target and limitations.
failureModes: Counting colleagues, conflicted respondents, or AI personas
Leading the participant or teaching the interface
Lowering the target after cancellations
Mixing prototype or question versions silently
limitations: One or two usable sessions are early/limited; three or four are partial directional under the #11 evidence model
Session counts never establish statistical confidence, prevalence, or representativeness

substitutes.name: One-to-one sessions plus deliberate observation and debrief checkpoints
substitutes.useWhen: A cross-functional Sprint watch party is unavailable.
substitutes.preserves: Individual observations remain traceable across sessions before synthesis.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Adapts team observation mechanics; the Sprint-book target remains five unless a deviation is recorded.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: A single human observer can miss signals, so contradictions and observation limitations must remain visible.

12-synthesis.title: Synthesise evidence
12-synthesis.whyItMatters: Traceable synthesis turns individual observations into bounded decision evidence while keeping contradictions and uncertainty intact.
12-synthesis.purpose: Compare observed customer evidence against the predefined questions and expose patterns, contradictions, outliers, and limitations.

methods.sprint-book: End-of-customer-day pattern review against sprint questions
methods.adaptive-design-sprint: Traceable question-by-question synthesis with independent critique

12-synthesis.humanEffort: Supply missing material session context and review evidence boundaries without repairing inconvenient results.
12-synthesis.humanAction: Confirm that no material session context is missing before the final decision.
aiRole: Synthesize only from the bounded summaries packet
Trace every claim to observation or inference IDs
Challenge cherry-picking and overclaiming
dependencies: At least one usable real session
whatGoodLooksLike: Every claim can be traced to included session evidence
Patterns, contradictions, outliers, quality limits, and partial counts are presented together
definitionOfDone: Every finding traces to included session evidence
Patterns, contradictions, outliers, strength, and gaps are visible
Partial recruitment remains partial under the #11 four-dimensional assessment
examples: Two of three participants hesitated at TASK-1; one completed directly. This is a directional usability signal, not prevalence.
failureModes: Rewriting the scorecard after results
Ignoring contradictory sessions
Inferring population confidence from a small directional sample
limitations: Partial or mixed-quality sessions narrow justified decisions
Synthesis cannot repair missing, unsuitable, or unusable sessions

substitutes.name: Summaries-only question review with separate critical pass
substitutes.useWhen: A team watch-party synthesis is unavailable.
substitutes.preserves: Question-by-question comparison, traceability, contradictions, and independent challenge.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Changes live group sensemaking into bounded sequential synthesis.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: Reduced human interpretive diversity can miss meanings; traceability keeps claims auditable.

13-outcome.title: Decide and hand off
13-outcome.whyItMatters: Separating process completion, evidence strength, and decision readiness prevents a finished sprint from being mistaken for a validated product.
13-outcome.purpose: Make a bounded human-owned decision that states what was learned, what remains unknown, and the next learning action.

methods.sprint-book: Decider review and post-sprint next-step decision
methods.adaptive-design-sprint: Evidence-limited outcome decision and owned handoff

13-outcome.humanEffort: Choose Proceed, Iterate, Pivot, Investigate, or Stop and own the dated next action.
13-outcome.humanAction: Select the evidence-bounded outcome, rationale, owner, and smallest next learning action.
aiRole: Present options with method, evidence, readiness, and limitation boundaries
Render the final private result and publication checklist links
dependencies: Traceable synthesis or explicit unvalidated closure
whatGoodLooksLike: The decision is no larger than the evidence supports
The portable result preserves method adaptations, evidence limits, risks, and the next learning action
definitionOfDone: Outcome and rationale are human-owned
Process completion, method fidelity, evidence strength, and decision readiness remain separate
Owners and dated actions are recorded
Private output validates before any separately sanitized #14-style results-site publication
examples: Iterate: correct the observed TASK-1 failure, then retest the same question with qualified participants before a larger investment.
failureModes: Calling partial evidence validation
Publishing the private workspace directly
Choosing Proceed, Iterate, or Pivot without usable real-customer evidence
limitations: The outcome is bounded by sample, protocol, prototype, and method limitations
Publication approval is separate from workspace validation and requires a sanitized results export

substitutes.name: Asynchronous evidence-bounded Decider review
substitutes.useWhen: A live team outcome meeting is unavailable.
substitutes.preserves: The human owns a documented choice with dissent, limitations, owner, and date.
substitutes.methodFidelityImpact: Compresses collective review but does not transfer the decision to AI.
substitutes.evidenceImpact: Missing stakeholder perspectives remain a decision-readiness limitation.
